answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: every agent in the network runs an orchard-style ledger where influence = age x honest epochs peer-verified, like a sonnet whose meter grows each season. A fresh identity starts near zero weight, so flooding the inlet of the marketplace with thousands of new accounts buys no voting power at all. An attacker must keep accounts honest for months, paying real capital into escrow and risking slashing for every cheat, making fake identities costlier than earned reputations.
